page_section_element_body.text: The role of motion in Aalto Design System is to help and guide the user. The aim is to make interactions easy to understand and create spatial awareness. Motion should also create a feeling of functional and polished interfaces.
Motion principles are the cornerstones of which every motion interaction should be based on.

body_text.text: Motion is used to help the user understand what will happen, what is happening and what has happened.
Motion is inherently digital and consequential from interaction to interaction.
Never flickering, never overwhelming and always with the option to be reduced.
Motion is used to highlight, emphasise and promote content.

All services designed with the Aalto design system should have the ability to correspond to operation system wide reduced motion settings. People with motion sensitivities should only encounter motion that is absolutely essential to understanding the interface, all other motion should be disabled.

page_section_element_body.text: A selection of effects can be used to move, reveal and present content. These are more limited when animating structural elements than content.

body_text.text: Moving an element along X- or Y-axis.
Increasing or decreasing the size of an element in X- or Y-axis or both.
Changing the color of an element, image or video.
Changing the opacity of an element.
Zooming in or out of an asset, such as image or video.
Altering the shape of a vector element such as an Icon.

page_section_element_body.text: The direction of motion is determined by the context of interactions. Direction is used to create and maintain a feeling of space and indicate what is about to happen.

body_text.text: Elements that reside in the top navigation area, such as search and menu, open by expanding down and close by contracting up.
Elements that reside in a bottom navigation area, open by expanding up and close by contracting down.
Elements that reside in a side navigation area, open by expanding right and close by contracting left.
Context specific elements such as modal windows and dialogs move toward the user when opened and move away when closed.
When moving forward current view will move to the left and when moving back to the right. A microinteraction of an icon will indicate this in a similar manner.
When a value increases an upwards motion is used and when it decreases a downwards motion is used.

page_section_element_body.text: Motion is used sparingly in web interfaces, while in mobile applications more motion can be added. There should always be an option to use reduced motion.
The main use cases for motion are transitions and micro interactions. It can also be used to highlight content.
Transitions are changes from one screen or page to another. In these cases motion is used to guide the user and help create spatial awareness inside an application.

body_text.text: Parallel elements live in the same plane and when moving between them there should be no sense of depth.
Contextual information is added on top of the initial screen keeping it partly visible.
In mobile applications a sense of space can be formed by moving elements on top of each other.

page_section_element_body.text: In parallel trasitions content can fade or be hidden and revealed by surfaces, but no sense of depth is created.
In contextual transitions surfaces and content appear from depth on top of the existing screen.
In mobile applications when a user delves deeper into the information spatial transition is used. This creates a sense of depth and direction.
Small, contained interactions that revolve around a single task or action are enhanced by motion.

body_text.text: Movement is used in indicators to inform about progress or status.
Movement is used to help user understand what is happening or going to happen.
Movement is used to catch the users attention.

page_section_element_body.text: A progress indicator tells the user that the system is active and processing even if nothing major is happening on the screen.
Small movement in icons can be used to indicate the interaction that happens on click.
Alerts and error messages use motion to get the users attention.

body_text.text: When developing user interface elements with motion, please refer to the motion tokens specification
